newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends higher, eyes cold front in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends higher, eyes cold front in Mexico.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures edged higher Wednesday, bolstered by concern a cold front approaching central Mexico posed a threat to the country's coffee crop, industry sources said.
The leading March contract rose 2.00 cents per lb on the day, to close at 111.90, just shy of its intraday peak of 112.15 cents.

Traders said worries that an Arctic airmass that had sent thermostats plummeting in the U.S. Midwest early this week might hit the northern fringes of Mexico's coffee belt touched off a round buying today.
"It initially ran up on the weather," said one trader. "You got more funds involved with the market."
Meteorologists were divided on the threat to Mexico's coffee, though most expected any damage to be fairly light.

Commodity funds and trade houses were steady buyers at the outset, lifting the market to its highs early in the day. But producers were quick to cash in on the higher prices, blocking any further advance, dealers said.
Mexico was reportedly among the sellers, along with Brazil and several Central American producers.
On the charts, March would need to punch through 112.50 cents to sustain the uptrend, with tough resistance noted at 115.00. To the downside, stops were said to be placed near 108.50 and 105 cents.
An estimated 6,774 lots were exchanged on the day.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
